notes: Activates the TRD-approved Hermes reasoning-runtime boundary while preserving DirectModelRuntime as a viable fallback.
Groq and OpenRouter credentials remain inside the Hermes service boundary and are never exposed to agents, domain state, browser code or committed configuration.
Hermes is constrained to zero tools, no persistent memory/context/skills and a Kairo-authenticated versioned invocation contract.
Normal routing is Groq primary with OpenRouter fallback; controlled benchmark mode is primary-only to preserve comparable evidence.
No database migration, release, deployment, provider-secret entry, VS-23 live activation or VS-24 promotion is authorized by this slice.

approvals.rationale: The owner explicitly selected Hermes with Groq and OpenRouter, created both provider keys privately, and instructed Go after the bounded Hermes integration direction and secret boundary were explained.

The approved TRD already defines Hermes as the preferred AgentRuntimePort implementation, DirectModelRuntime fallback, provider-neutral model access, secret isolation, zero agent publishing authority and auditable model cost. This slice does not broaden those policies.

The owner's Go instruction authorizes bounded implementation of the agreed Hermes runtime integration. Merge, release, deployment, provider-secret entry and production enablement remain separate approvals.
Exact candidate SHA and complete CI/security evidence are required before certification.
